learningObjective: Order the tiers of a modern GPU memory hierarchy by latency, bandwidth and capacity, and identify design consequences.
stem: Which statements about the NVIDIA GPU memory hierarchy (Ampere/Hopper) are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Because L2 has higher bandwidth than HBM, an inference kernel that fits in L2 sees roughly HBM-tier throughput; L2 acts only as a latency shield, not a bandwidth multiplier.
Latency ordering (fastest to slowest): registers → shared memory / L1 → L2 → HBM. Latency grows by roughly an order of magnitude across the last two boundaries.
Capacity ordering (largest to smallest): HBM → L2 → shared memory (per SM) → register file (per SM). HBM dwarfs on-chip storage by several orders of magnitude.
Aggregate bandwidth ordering, summed across all SMs, is: register file ≫ shared memory ≫ L2 ≫ HBM. On-chip tiers close to compute are the widest.

explanation: A: standard latency ordering; each on-chip step is faster than off-chip. B: HBM is orders of magnitude larger than on-chip caches (tens of GB vs KB-MB). C: aggregate on-chip bandwidths scale with number of SMs, greatly exceeding HBM's bandwidth (~2 TB/s A100). D is wrong: L2 acts as both a latency shield and a bandwidth multiplier when data fits and is reused — L2 aggregate bandwidth is well above HBM.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: L2 provides substantial bandwidth uplift over HBM when data is reused; it is not merely a latency shield.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: register < shared/L1 < L2 < HBM in latency; on-chip tiers dominate for locality.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: capacity increases moving away from compute.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: on-chip aggregate bandwidth greatly exceeds HBM; this is why kernels use shared memory and register-file reuse.

assumptions: Modern NVIDIA GPU (Ampere/Hopper) with the standard R/S/L2/HBM hierarchy.
Aggregate bandwidth is measured summed across all SMs where applicable.
nonImplications: Does not imply every kernel benefits from L2 residency; write-back patterns and capacity misses can reduce L2 effectiveness.
Does not imply register-file size is negligible per SM; it is comparable to shared memory in capacity but with per-thread lifetime.

distractorRationales.A: Reduces L2's role to latency reduction only, ignoring bandwidth aspect.
